From 8a768552f7a8276fb9e01d49773d2094ace7c8f1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Heitor Alves de Siqueira <halves@igalia.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:27:28 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] usb: usbtmc: Flush anchored URBs in usbtmc_release

When calling usbtmc_release, pending anchored URBs must be flushed or
killed to prevent use-after-free errors (e.g. in the HCD giveback
path). Call usbtmc_draw_down() to allow anchored URBs to be completed.

Fixes: 4f3c8d6eddc2 ("usb: usbtmc: Support Read Status Byte with SRQ per file")
Reported-by: syzbot+9a3c54f52bd1edbd975f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=9a3c54f52bd1edbd975f
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Heitor Alves de Siqueira <halves@igalia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260312-usbtmc-flush-release-v1-1-5755e9f4336f@igalia.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c b/drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c
index d39bbfd7fd18..bd9347804dec 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c
@@ -254,6 +254,9 @@ static int usbtmc_release(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
 	list_del(&file_data->file_elem);
 
 	spin_unlock_irq(&file_data->data->dev_lock);
+
+	/* flush anchored URBs */
+	usbtmc_draw_down(file_data);
 	mutex_unlock(&file_data->data->io_mutex);
 
 	kref_put(&file_data->data->kref, usbtmc_delete);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

### Modifications in each file:

- **`drivers/usb/class/usbtmc.c`**:
  - In the `usbtmc_release()` function, added a call to `usbtmc_draw_down(file_data)` after releasing the `data->dev_lock` spinlock and before releasing the `data->io_mutex` mutex.
  - The added line is: `/* flush anchored URBs */ usbtmc_draw_down(file_data);`

### Relationship between modifications:

- The change is contained entirely in one file and addresses a use-after-free bug by ensuring that all pending anchored URBs are properly flushed (completed or killed) before the file data structure is fully released. 
- The `usbtmc_draw_down()` function is already defined in the same driver and is responsible for waiting until all URBs associated with a given `file_data` have finished. Placing this call in `usbtmc_release` prevents the HCD's giveback path from accessing freed memory, thus fixing the race condition reported by syzbot.

Here is the commit message:
usb: usbtmc: Flush anchored URBs in usbtmc_release

When calling usbtmc_release, pending anchored URBs must be flushed or
killed to prevent use-after-free errors (e.g. in the HCD giveback
path). Call usbtmc_draw_down() to allow anchored URBs to be completed.

Fixes: 4f3c8d6eddc2 ("usb: usbtmc: Support Read Status Byte with SRQ per file")
Reported-by: syzbot+9a3c54f52bd1edbd975f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=9a3c54f52bd1edbd975f
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Heitor Alves de Siqueira <halves@igalia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260312-usbtmc-flush-release-v1-1-5755e9f4336f@igalia.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
In usbtmc_release(), pending anchored URBs were not flushed (killed or waited for completion) before the file data structure was freed. This allowed a URB to complete via the HCD giveback path after the associated memory was released, leading to a use-after-free error.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int usbtmc_release(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
 {
 	struct usbtmc_file_data *file_data = file->private_data;
 
 	/* prevent IO _AND_ usbtmc_interrupt */
 	mutex_lock(&file_data->data->io_mutex);
 	spin_lock_irq(&file_data->data->dev_lock);
 
 	list_del(&file_data->file_elem);
 
 	spin_unlock_irq(&file_data->data->dev_lock);
+
+	/* flush anchored URBs */
+	usbtmc_draw_down(file_data);
 	mutex_unlock(&file_data->data->io_mutex);
 
 	kref_put(&file_data->data->kref, usbtmc_delete);
 	file_data->data = NULL;
 	kfree(file_data);
 	return 0;
 }
